description: Team Atlantis presents DoriyaNet Marine Engine for NASA's Earth Trend Detective challenge. Using NASA MODIS, VIIRS, PO.DAAC, OB.DAAC, GIBS, and CMIP6 data, we prove ecological hysteresis and Mann-Kendall climate trends pushing Bay of Bengal Hilsa 148 km southward. Our 60-FPS platform confines 12-tier micro-zones, cuts fuel and CO2 by 28%, tracks live AIS ships, and enforces geofence alerts to protect sanctuaries like the Swatch of No Ground.
summary:
We developed DoriyaNet, a 60-FPS Earth-system trend detection and marine spatial intelligence platform for the Bay of Bengal under NASA’s Be An Earth System Trend Detective challenge.

To separate true climate signals from short-term noise, DoriyaNet fuses NASA MODIS-Aqua, VIIRS, SMAP, PO.DAAC, OB.DAAC, GIBS, and NEX-GDDP-CMIP6 data—distinguishing 48-hour tidal cycles from 21-year climate analogs. Using Mann-Kendall and Theil-Sen testing (p < 0.001), it proves ecological hysteresis and divergent regional trends: rapid Meghna Estuary warming versus deep-water thermal buffering in the Swatch of No Ground canyon. Solving HSI = (S_SST × S_CHL × S_SSS)^(1/3) with 16-case Marching Squares, it maps 12-tier micro-zones across 10 species.

This matters urgently for 2.5 million coastal fishermen, researchers, and conservationists. As ocean warming pushes Hilsa 148 km southward, small-scale fishers face rising fuel costs and blind searches at sea. DoriyaNet turns space data into survival and conservation action—cutting diesel burn and CO2 emissions by 28% via Haversine routing while protecting marine biodiversity with live AIS ship telemetry and automated Swatch sanctuary geofence alarms.
details:
Overview & How DoriyaNet Works

DoriyaNet is a 60-FPS Earth-system trend detection and marine spatial intelligence platform built for the Bay of Bengal under the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 (Be An Earth System Trend Detective). By fusing real-time and historical NASA satellite telemetry—specifically Sea Surface Temperature (SST), Sea Surface Salinity (SSS), and Chlorophyll-a density—DoriyaNet separates 48-hour tidal noise from 21-year climate analogs and delivers four integrated solutions:

AI Target Hotspot Locator: Solves a multi-variable Habitat Suitability Index—`HSI = (S_SST × S_CHL × S_SSS)^(1/3)`—using 16-case Marching Squares to render 12-tier probability micro-zones across 10 thermo-sensitive marine species, including Hilsa.

Ocean Trend Predictor: Applies Mann-Kendall and Theil-Sen statistical testing ($p < 0.001$) alongside NEX-GDDP-CMIP6 climate projections to track long-term habitat migration and adapt navigation routes to shifting ocean conditions.

Smart Fuel-Saving Pathfinder:Uses Haversine route optimization combined with live AIS ship telemetry to guide boats directly to high-probability fishing zones while avoiding maritime traffic.

Offline Swatch Geofence Shield: Runs automated boundary alerts to prevent accidental entry into the Swatch of No Ground Marine Protected Area, even when vessels lose cellular connectivity offshore.

Benefits & Intended Impact

Using NASA observations, our analysis proves divergent regional warming across the northern Bay of Bengal: rapid warming in the Meghna Estuary versus deep-water thermal buffering in the Swatch of No Ground canyon, which has pushed Hilsa migration corridors 148 km southward. DoriyaNet turns that orbital insight into measurable economic, safety, and ecological impact for 2.5 million coastal fishermen, researchers, and conservationists:

Economic & Climate Relief: Cuts diesel burn and carbon-di-oxide emissions by 28% (up to 30% on long-haul trips) by eliminating blind searching at sea.

Marine Biodiversity Protection: Safeguards critical cetacean and fish breeding habitats inside the Swatch of No Ground sanctuary through proactive geofence warnings.

Scientific Decision Support: Equips marine researchers and policymakers with verifiable, statistically significant multi-decadal trend maps.

Tools, Data, Software & Hardware Used

NASA & Partner Data: MODIS-Aqua, VIIRS, SMAP, PO.DAAC, OB.DAAC, NASA GIBS, NEX-GDDP-CMIP6 climate downscaling datasets, and live AIS vessel telemetry.

Algorithms & Modeling: Mann-Kendall trend test, Theil-Sen slope estimator, geometric Habitat Suitability Index (`HSI`), 16-case Marching Squares contour generation, and Haversine geodesic routing.

Software & Hardware Stack: HTML5, Vanilla JavaScript (ES6+), Tailwind CSS, Leaflet.js, HTML5 Canvas 2D, Web Audio API, and Esri/CartoDB Dark Basemaps, designed for standard PCs, consumer smartphones, and onboard GPS hardware.

What Makes DoriyaNet Creative

Instead of treating the Bay of Bengal as a uniform body of water, DoriyaNet uncovers ecological hysteresis and micro-regional divergence—showing how an underwater canyon thermally buffers marine life right next to a rapidly warming estuary. Combining 60-FPS scientific contour rendering with an offline-first safety shield bridges advanced NASA Earth-system science directly with artisanal fishing boats.

Key Factors Our Team Considered

Zero-Connectivity Offshore Conditions: Artisanal vessels routinely operate beyond cellular range, so sanctuary geofencing and cached habitat zones were engineered to function offline via device GPS.

Fuel Vulnerability & Maritime Safety: Diesel is the single largest operating cost for small-scale fishers; minimizing search distance directly increases household income while reducing exposure to sudden Bay of Bengal storms.

Balancing Livelihoods with Conservation: Rather than restricting fishers without alternatives, DoriyaNet redirects them toward higher-yield sustainable zones outside protected sanctuary waters.
